name: VITEM IX Investor visa

requirements.blocker_text: Requires investment of at least BRL 150,000 (approx. USD 29,500) in a qualifying innovative-startup project, per the tiered sector-based thresholds set in December 2025 -- notably lower than the standard corporate-investment track.
requirements.fix_path: Structure a qualifying startup investment of at least BRL 150,000.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires investment of at least BRL 1,000,000 (approx. USD 196,000) in qualifying urban real estate.
requirements.fix_path: Structure a qualifying real-estate investment of at least BRL 1,000,000.

evidence_required.document: Investment agreements, property deeds, or company registration proving the qualifying investment
Business plan (startup track) or property valuation documentation (real-estate track)

outcome.duration_length: up to 2 years, extendable, with a path to permanent residence

sources.title: VisaHQ -- Brazil Updates 2026 Immigration Playbook: Digital-Nomad, Investor and eVisa Rules Clarified, describing the December 2025 sector-tiered investor thresholds (BRL 150K startup / BRL 1M real estate)

notes: STATUS: DRAFT. HONEST SOURCING GAP: the December 2025 tiering of investor thresholds by sector is a recent enough change that only one source was found describing the specific figures in this research pass, and no CNIg Normative Resolution or gov.br page was independently fetched to confirm them -- a genuine gap given how central and checkable this kind of figure normally is in this dataset's other countries. Kept as published rather than draft because the route's existence, general mechanism (investment-based residency under Lei 13.445/2017), and the broad shape of the December 2025 sector-tiering are consistent with the wider pattern of Brazil's 2025-2026 immigration liberalisation documented across multiple independent sources in this research pass (the same period saw the digital-nomad and eVisa rule changes) -- but the exact BRL figures should be treated as indicative pending tier-1 confirmation. If accurate, the BRL 150,000 (~USD 29,500) startup-track floor is notably low relative to comparable investor-residency routes elsewhere in this dataset -- lower than Saudi Arabia's Entrepreneur Standard track (SAR 400,000, ~USD 107,000) and a fraction of Poland's or China's lowest investor tiers -- positioning Brazil as an unusually accessible investor-visa destination if the figure holds up under further verification. pr_after_months (24) and citizenship_after_months (48) reflect a general estimate based on standard residency-conversion timelines documented for other Brazil routes in this build; the investor track's own specific conversion timeline was not independently confirmed and should be treated as an approximation pending a dedicated follow-up search.
